page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.1-4 is an ARM-based compute instance built on the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor architecture. The configuration supplies 2 dedicated physical cores addressing 2 vCPUs at a single thread per core, avoiding hardware multithreading contention. System memory is sized at 4.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The instance provides dedicated ARM64 compute capacity without bundled local disk storage or hardware GPU acceleration. Persistent storage must be attached via networked cloud block volumes. Network configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the hardware utilizes dedicated single-threaded Ampere cores, execution threads operate without resource sharing across logical threads on the same physical core.

With its compute-focused memory allocation and dedicated ARM64 cores, VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.1-4 provides predictable efficiency for light to medium scale workloads. The architecture suits ARM-native application building, CI/CD pipeline agents, microservices, web serving tiers, and containerized utilities that fit within a 4.0 GB memory footprint and do not require local NVMe drives.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.1-4 is an ARM64 cloud instance configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs on 2 physical cores utilizing Ampere AmpereOne-M processors. Operating at one thread per core, the instance provides isolated execution units paired with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes no hardware GPU acceleration and contains no local storage, requiring attached network block storage for persistent data. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is provided for external network access. This hardware profile delivers predictable compute performance and cost efficiency for lightweight compute-bound services, web servers, continuous integration tasks, container deployments, and ARM-targeted development environments that do not require high memory density or local disk I/O.
